correctness.rationale: Exact two-generator Hilbert-series identity gives every nontrivial root-of-unity value with exactly one removable generator factor. The discrete inverse transform of 1/(1-zeta^b) at d-th roots is ((d-1)/2 - rem_d(b^{-1}r)); genus changes by m(a-1)/2. Coprimality of d and e gives simultaneous CRT extremes. Nonresonant denominator moduli are >=4/m, so the residual Fourier range is <=m/2+m^2/4. The source-free DP checker verified 6,266 histograms, 4,383 steps in each direction and 340 progression cases; these are tests, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural, previously unresolved quantitative question is how residue imbalance changes when a generator is not a modular unit. The theorem proves a complete exact affine response for every valid generator increment and a sharp principal range coefficient for every modulus and generator pair; the two coprime resonance moduli contribute additively by CRT. This makes the bounded-versus-growing transition quantitative and handles both generators simultaneously, far beyond isolated numerical table values or a routine fixed-parameter recomputation.
